note: The OSS-Fuzz testcase bytes are passed directly to the sudoers parser as an in-memory input stream.
The first parser initialization registers the parser leak cleanup handler and initializes parsing state for the fuzzed input.
The malformed defaults and command-option text in the testcase causes allocated token strings such as runchroot or runcwd values to be tracked in parser_leak_list.

The grammar transfers command-option strings out of the generic leak-tracked pointer set while building command specifications. The vulnerable state can leave ownership duplicated across parser cleanup structures after malformed command-option syntax.
The malformed input builds partially-owned command/member structures before the parser reports an error.
After the parse, the fuzz harness calls init_parser(NULL), which first frees the parse tree accumulated before the parse error.
The same cleanup call then drains parser_leak_list for allocations still considered unowned after the failed parse.
Because parser_leak_init has already run once for this process, the second init invokes parser_leak_free immediately.
A member still present in the leak list points into an object already released during parse-tree cleanup, producing the heap double-free reported by ASAN in parser_leak_free.
